paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole passage is shouting at us: your words, your hands and your habits are never small. A quick handshake on a pledge can trap you, and the writer says to get free fast: "Go, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor" (Proverbs 6:3). Then comes the ant, who gets her work done with no commander and no overseer, preparing her provisions in summer (Proverbs 6:7-8). Wisdom is doing the right thing before somebody makes you.

Now look at the rest. The slacker says, "A little sleep, a little slumber," and the writer warns that poverty "will come upon you like a robber" (Proverbs 6:10-11). The wicked man has deceit in his heart, and he "continually sows discord" (Proverbs 6:14). Little choices, repeated, grow up into big harvests, and I think that's why the writer keeps pointing at what we plant.

And then the list, friend. Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands, a heart, feet, a false witness, and "one who stirs up discord among brothers" (Proverbs 6:17-19). That's a whole body, head to toe, and the LORD cares what every part of it is doing. So give Him your eyes, your tongue, your hands and your feet, and let them build peace instead of drama. I'd rather have a bakery full of peace than a pile of crumbs, baker.
